instruction: more_itertools.zip_broadcast opens each iterable argument twice: it calls iter() once to decide whether the argument is iterable and again to iterate it. An input whose __iter__ may run only once (for example one that raises RuntimeError when opened a second time) therefore fails, with or without strict=True. Make zip_broadcast call iter() on each argument once and iterate that iterator. Everything else stays as it is: str and bytes (or the given scalar_types) and objects that aren't iterable are repeated as scalars, scalar_types=None treats strings as iterables, and strict=True still raises when the iterables have different lengths. For example zip_broadcast('label', source) with a single-use source of [1, 2] gives [('label', 1), ('label', 2)], and an empty single-use source gives [].
